description: Tools a job needs: owned, borrowed, hired or still to buy. Separate from project_items (37) because a tool is USED, not consumed. Import FORTIETH (needs user_projects)
notes: Why not just an item: an item is consumed and costs what it costs. A tool is used and handed back. The four states below have four different money consequences, and a list that cannot tell them apart cannot answer 'what do I still need to get, and what will it cost me'.

status: own = it is in the shed, costs nothing. borrow = someone is lending it, costs nothing but has to go back. hire = costs rate x days. buy = a one-off cost. Only hire and buy add anything to a budget.
hire_rate is PER DAY and hire_days multiplies it. Storing a single total instead would lose the two numbers people actually negotiate and check.
source is who or where: 'Dad', 'HSS Hire', a shop. Free text, because the next job's answer is never in a list you wrote in advance.
return_by matters for a borrowed tool and nothing else. A borrowed tool with no return date is how friendships end.
needed_by is when the job needs it in hand, which is what an 'order this now' list sorts by.
project_id and task_id are TEXT holding row ids, as everywhere else.

user_id.description: Xano user id as a string. EVERY read filters on this

task_id.description: Optional: the task that needs it

milestone_id.description: Optional: the stage it is needed for

status.description: own and borrow cost nothing; hire and buy are money

purchase_cost.description: One-off cost when it is being bought

hire_rate.description: Cost per day when it is being hired

hire_days.description: How many days it is hired for

currency.description: ISO code. Blank means the project's own

needed_by.description: When the job needs it in hand

return_by.description: When a borrowed or hired tool goes back

in_hand.description: It is here now. A hired tool can be in hand and still cost money
